text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game where each token I contribute to the group pool pays back 0.3 to every member, so 1.2 total is generated but I only recoup 0.3 of what I give. Individually, keeping tokens (1 point each) dominates contributing, yet full cooperation would maximize the group's total payoff.

Weighing it out, contributing always costs me more than it returns individually, so the dominant strategy is to keep everything. I'll go with contributing 0 this round and briefly explain my reasoning rather than test cooperation first.

reply.thinking:

I'll go with a moderate contribution of 10 for round one, testing the group's willingness to cooperate without fully committing to it.
